recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if FHIR-I later decides to split $convert into narrower operations or define additional conversion parameters.
issue_request: FHIR-13888 was a Published FHIR-core change request resolved Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked for an operation, originally proposed as $convert-format, that would let a server convert a FHIR instance from one format to another.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites svn revision 14068. Git-svn commit b2cfcb7d23 added the Resource spreadsheet row for a draft/FMM 1 system operation with code convert, single Resource input/output parameters, and conversion prose; 9af457e51d added request/response examples. The source later migrated to source/resource/operationdefinition-Resource-convert.xml and source/resource/list-Resource-operations.xml.
additional_context: The linked Zulip discussion described GF#13888 as creating $convert for JSON/XML conversion and broader draft experimentation, explaining the accepted name. Later Published issues refined the same operation without reversing it: FHIR-37983 renamed input/output parameters to resource/return, and FHIR-20912 clarified the HTTP version-parameter rule for operations such as $convert.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current build-scope source defines OperationDefinition/Resource-convert with code convert, system=true, type=false, instance=false, draft status, FMM 1, a required Resource input named resource, a required Resource output named return, examples for XML-to-JSON and version conversion, and an HTTP-page cross-reference.

related_jiras.note: Clarified that differing Accept and Content-Type FHIR version parameters are allowed when invoking a version-conversion operation such as $convert.
Renamed $convert parameters from input/output to resource/return, explaining a current-source difference from the original spreadsheet application.
Broad typo cleanup touched the $convert page but did not change the operation requested by FHIR-13888.
